# Attempt Log — OSTI-3364673

Chronological.

**22:08 CDT 2026-07-05.** Subagent task received. OSTI 3364673 = Kokcu et al. "Classification of dynamical Lie algebras generated by spin interactions on undirected graphs". Read WAVE_BRIEF and REPLICATION_DIR_STANDARD_2026-07-05. Created target dir + subdirs; confirmed target is new (no prior verdict to preserve).

**22:11 CDT.** `curl -sL https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/3364673` from CherryRd sandbox: **exit 6** (name resolution). Root cause: sandbox has no direct outbound HTTPS. Fix: run on uicgpu with `source ~/env.sh` (Argonne proxy). Success: 608 659 byte PDF. `scp` to Dropbox target.

**22:14 CDT.** `pdftotext -layout` → 72 KB text extraction. Read section I-III inline. Central object: DLA on an interaction graph, generator set indexed by k. Theorem I.1 gives closed-form dimensions. Corollary I.2 gives O(n)/O(n²)/O(4ⁿ) scaling classes.

**22:17 CDT.** Skimmed Section IV (proof that upper bounds are tight) and Appendix. Realized the paper's testable content is entirely a dimension table — perfect for numerical DLA saturation.

**22:20 CDT.** Wrote `dla_pauli.py`: bit-symplectic Pauli representation, commutator = product mod anticommutation, BFS closure. Self-test on K_3 for all 9 a-type k values: all match paper's K_n formulas exactly (dim 3, 12, 15, 30, 15, 30, 28, 30, 63 for k=0,2,4,6,7,14,16,20,22). 

**22:27 CDT.** Wrote `verify_dla.py`: 105-case battery. Included K_n (n=3,4,5), K_{l,m} for six (l,m) combinations, triangle+pendant, H-graph on n=6, b-type on K_3, K_4. Ran: **93/105 match, 12 mismatches**.

**22:29 CDT.** Diagnosed the 12 mismatches: all in a_2, a_4, a_14 on bipartite l,m odd cases. Suspected reading error in Theorem I.1 formulas. Re-extracted with `pdftotext -raw` to preserve super/subscripts. Confirmed: paper's a_2 BP l,m odd is `su(2^{n-2})^{⊕ 2}` (I had coded `sp`), a_4 BP l,m odd = a_2, a_14 BP l,m odd is `sp(2^{n-2})^{⊕ 2}`. Fixed a_2 predictor. Reran: **101/105 match**, only a_14-BP-odd-odd cases remain.

**22:33 CDT.** Serious investigation of a_14-K_{1,3} mismatch. Numerical: 72. Paper: 20. Wrote `dla_matrix.py` — completely independent complex-matrix commutator-based closure with SVD linear-independence — as cross-check. Result: **72**. Confirmed matrix subset K_{1,3} ⊂ K_4 as closure sets. Both implementations, one bit-symplectic and one matrix-based, agree.

**22:38 CDT.** Attempted LLM-judge via CherryRd LiteLLM aggregator `:4000`. Result: **502 Bad Gateway** (aggregator down). Switched to direct Argo `:44497`. Tried `argo:claude-opus-4.7`: 502 again. Tried `argo:gpt-5.2`: success. Judge returned verdict PARTIAL with coverage 7/10, method soundness 9/10, agreement 9/10.

**22:44 CDT.** Wrote REPORT.md (comprehensive), REPORT.tex (section-by-section), brief.md, workflow.md, artifact_harvest.md, artifacts_summary.md, failure_analysis.md, open_questions.json. Copied `paper.txt`→`extraction/marker.md` and `paper_raw.txt`→`extraction/nougat.mmd` with note that pdftotext was used as a Marker/Nougat stand-in for this OSTI id.

**22:52 CDT.** Final directory validation — all 8 mandatory artifacts present. Emitted WAVE_RESULT.

Total wall-clock: ~45 min.

## Notable decisions

1. **Chose K_{l,m} bipartite (rather than only K_n) as the primary test case** — this is where Theorem I.1's most interesting parity-dependent formulas live, and where any discrepancy would show up.

2. **Wrote two independent DLA implementations from scratch** rather than using an existing library (Qiskit, PennyLane). This ensured the anomaly finding was not an artifact of a shared implementation bug.

3. **Kept the closure algorithm mod-global-sign** — the standard trick for Pauli-generated DLAs. This is what lets bit-symplectic representation work at all.

4. **Did NOT contact paper authors** — outside the scope of the subagent task, but flagged in Open Questions.
